design_version.description: Design record format version this document conforms to.

AppDesign.description: Design record of one interactive data application: its needs organised by the four perspectives, the options considered, the choices made and the traces from each need to the specification elements that answer it. It is a proposal until its choices are bound by rulings; it never records its own acceptance.

Ruling.description: Record of an attributable decision. An agent may transcribe an evidenced decision but cannot originate one; status proposed carries no authority.

TaskGoal.description: Why the user performs the task (Brehmer & Munzner 2013 "why"; Schulz et al. 2013 goal).

SearchMode.description: Brehmer & Munzner's search modes, defined by whether the target and its location are known.

QueryAction.description: Brehmer & Munzner's query actions, ordered by cardinality.

TaskTarget.description: What the task is about in the data (Munzner's targets; Schulz et al.'s characteristics).

Cardinality.description: How many instances the task concerns (Schulz et al. 2013).

AnalyticTemplate.description: Amar, Eagan & Stasko's ten low-level analytic tasks, usable as question templates with slots.

DecisionStage.description: Simon's decision stages as used by Dimara & Stasko (2022); the choice itself stays the decision maker's act.

LocalTask.description: This ontology's own facet, for tasks the cited typologies lack. It is not one of Schulz et al.'s adaptation operations, which keep their five dimensions unchanged. Deciding is not a task here: it is a Decision, made by a person.

MeasureType.description: Kinds of performance measure in structured decision making.

DataCharacteristic.description: Characteristics of data that make a design pattern applicable or inapplicable.

AppRole.description: What the application contributes to a decision. The application never decides; the decision stays with the decision maker (thesis Framework §2.5). Structured decision making draws the same line: "Science can quantify risk and tradeoffs, but not determine which risks and tradeoffs are worth taking".

Detectability.description: How readily the intended users would notice a wrong answer.

ChoiceCategory.description: Consequential choices change meaning, results or reliance; each binds only under a made ruling whose scope names it (one checkpoint ruling may name several). Presentation and routine choices may bind under a made delegation. The category is the author's proposal, shown to the human at the design checkpoint.

Standing.description: Thesis epistemic labels (Chapter 3 §3.2.2); useful where a consumer needs them, not exhaustive.

ConsequenceTier.description: Proportionate-review tiers, keyed to intended reliance, not app type.

Archetype.description: Composable application patterns found in a survey of public data apps.

ValueSemantics.description: Meaning of values that affects valid operations (e.g. circular values in a linear correlation).
